findings.title: Unconditional `organization_context.member.has_global_access` crashes when the caller has no membership
findings.description: `enable_advanced` is computed on every request, not only when `optimized_pagination=true` is passed. `RpcUserOrganizationContext.member` is declared `RpcOrganizationMember | None` (`src/sentry/organizations/services/organization/model.py:344-346`, "member can be None when the given user_id does not have membership"). For any non-superuser caller with no member row, `request.user.is_superuser` is falsy and `.member.has_global_access` raises `AttributeError`, giving a 500. Token or API-key callers with `org:write` are the likely case, though I did not trace the auth classes to confirm which callers reach this. This is a regression on the previously working `DateTimePaginator` path. Guard for `None` and compute the gate only when the flag is requested.

findings.title: `OptimizedCursorPaginator` is incompatible with a datetime ordering key and fails on any non-empty result
findings.description:
The endpoint passes `order_by="-datetime"`, and `AuditLogEntry.datetime` is a `DateTimeField` (`src/sentry/models/auditlogentry.py:69`). Two things break:
- **Key computation:** `get_item_key` is copied from the numeric `Paginator` and calls `math.floor(value)` / `math.ceil(value)` on a `datetime`, which raises `TypeError`. `build_cursor` calls `key(results[0])` whenever there is at least one row (`src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:121-122`), so the first page of any org with audit entries returns 500.
- **Cursor value:** `value_from_cursor` returns the raw integer, which `build_queryset` binds into `datetime <= %s` (`src/sentry/api/paginator.py:122-126`). That compares a timestamp column to an integer instead of converting from epoch-ms as `DateTimePaginator.value_from_cursor` does (lines 238-241).

Cursors issued by the `DateTimePaginator` branch are therefore not usable with `optimized_pagination=true`.

findings.title: Negative-offset slicing is not supported by Django; a crafted cursor yields an unhandled 500
findings.description: The comment claims "The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically". As far as I know, `QuerySet.__getitem__` in the pinned Django 5.2.1 raises `ValueError("Negative indexing is not supported.")` for a negative slice start; Django's source is not vendored here, so I could not confirm it in-repo. `Cursor.from_string` accepts negative offsets (`src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:59`), so `?optimized_pagination=true&cursor=0:-1:0` reaches `queryset[-1:stop]`. `Endpoint.paginate` only catches `BadPaginationError` (`src/sentry/api/base.py:540`), so the error surfaces as a 500 rather than a 400. The advertised feature cannot function; it only adds a user-triggerable error path. Reject negative offsets at cursor parsing or raise `BadPaginationError`, as `OffsetPaginator` already does.

findings.title: `BasePaginator` still passes negative offsets through for `is_prev` cursors, with a comment that contradicts the code
findings.description: `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` clamps only forward cursors. A prev cursor with a negative offset (e.g. `123:-5:1`) still reaches `queryset[-5:stop]` and fails in every `BasePaginator` subclass (`Paginator`, `DateTimePaginator`, and others). The comment says the change "allow[s] negative offsets" and that this "is safe because the underlying queryset will handle boundary conditions"; the code does the opposite for forward cursors and is unsafe for prev cursors. The trim check at line 192 still uses the unclamped `offset`. Clamp or reject consistently and correct the comment.

findings.title: Authorization gate uses raw `is_superuser` and `has_global_access`, neither of which means "authorized administrator"
findings.description: `request.user.is_superuser` is the stored user flag, not an active superuser session. The permission class for this same endpoint uses `is_active_superuser(request)` (`src/sentry/api/bases/organization.py:124`). `has_global_access` is a team/project visibility attribute, not an admin role; I believe it is true for ordinary members in open-membership orgs, but did not trace where it is set. The comment "Enable advanced pagination features for authorized administrators" therefore overstates the gate. The feature is advertised in-code as enabling "access to data beyond normal pagination bounds" (`src/sentry/api/paginator.py:878-879`). The gate should use `is_active_superuser(request)` and a role or scope check, or be removed along with the feature.

findings.title: No tests for the new paginator, the new query parameter, or the changed `BasePaginator` offset handling
findings.description: `OptimizedCursorPaginator`, `optimized_pagination` and `enable_advanced_features` appear only in the two changed source files. `tests/sentry/api/endpoints/test_organization_auditlogs.py` has no case for the optimized branch, for a caller with no membership, or for negative cursors. A single endpoint test with `optimized_pagination=true` and one audit entry would have exposed the `TypeError` above. The shared `BasePaginator.get_result` change also ships without a test in `tests/sentry/api/test_paginator.py`.

findings.title: `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` duplicates `BasePaginator.get_result` almost line for line
findings.description: About 65 lines are copied from `BasePaginator.get_result` (lines 136-215), differing only in the slice-start branch. Both arms of the `if/else` at 877-886 end in the same `stop`/`results` statements. `get_item_key` and `value_from_cursor` are also verbatim copies of `Paginator` (lines 221-227). Any future fix to the base must be mirrored by hand. If the behaviour were valid, it belongs in a small overridable hook on `BasePaginator`.

findings.title: Comments and docstring claim performance and safety properties the code does not have
findings.description: The class docstring promises an "Optimized query path for large datasets" and "efficient reverse pagination", but the query is identical to the base `OFFSET/LIMIT` slice; nothing is optimized. Line 879 ("This is safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level") and line 876 are unsupported assertions on a security-sensitive endpoint. The comment added at `src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:26-27` describes a behaviour change ("Allow negative offsets") on a line that did not change (`self.offset = int(offset)`).

findings.title: Style nits in the changed hunks
findings.description: Trailing whitespace at `organization_auditlogs.py:72` and `:89` (`order_by="-datetime", `), whitespace in the docstring at `paginator.py:824,827`, and three blank lines before the class plus a trailing blank line at EOF (`paginator.py:818-820`, `912`). These would fail the project's formatter and flake8 pre-commit hooks.
